answer:
The Great Sphinx of Giza is primarily carved from **limestone**. 

Limestone is a sedimentary rock composed mainly of the mineral **calcite** (calcium carbonate, CaCO₃). Specifically, the Sphinx was carved from the Middle Eocene limestone of the Mokattam Formation on the Giza Plateau. This bedrock formation dates back approximately 50 million years and was part of an ancient sea floor before being exposed by geological processes.
